bugs.summary: Memory leak in `scan()` when a field fails type conversion
bugs.creator: kevinushey

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
Created attachment 3773
Candidate patch.

## Summary

`scan()` leaks its internal line buffer (an 8 KB `R_StringBuffer`) every
time it aborts on a malformed field. `scanVector()` and `scanFrame()`
allocate the buffer with `R_AllocStringBuffer()` and free it with
`R_FreeStringBuffer()` only on their normal return paths. When a value
cannot be converted to the requested type, `extractItem()` calls
`error()`, which `longjmp`s out of the function and skips the free, so
the buffer is leaked.

Because `read.table()` / `read.csv()` are built on `scan()`, this is
reachable from ordinary data-reading code: every failed parse of an
untrusted or malformed input leaks ~8 KB. A long-running process that
repeatedly reads malformed input accumulates these leaks.

Severity: low. It is a memory leak, not a memory-safety error — no crash
or corruption. The practical impact is unbounded memory growth in a
persistent process that keeps parsing malformed input.

## Affected code

`src/main/scan.c`, `scanVector()` (as of r89873). The buffer is
allocated once, up front:

```
static SEXP scanVector(SEXPTYPE type, R_xlen_t maxitems, R_xlen_t maxlines,
                       int flush, SEXP stripwhite, int blskip, LocalData *d)
{
    ...
    R_StringBuffer strBuf = {NULL, 0, MAXELTSIZE};
    ...
    R_AllocStringBuffer(0, &strBuf);              /* line 571: malloc */
    PROTECT(ans = allocVector(type, blocksize));
    ...
    for (;;) {
        ...
        buffer = fillBuffer(type, strip, &bch, d, &strBuf);
        ...
        extractItem(buffer, ans, n, d);           /* line 617: may error() */
        ...
    }
    ...
    R_FreeStringBuffer(&strBuf);                   /* lines 638/643/674 */
    return bns;
}
```

`extractItem()` throws on a type mismatch via `expected()`:

```
NORET static R_INLINE void expected(char *what, char *got, LocalData *d)
{
    ...
    error(_("scan() expected '%s', got '%s'"), what, got);   /* line 494 */
}
```

The `error()` at line 494 `longjmp`s straight past the
`R_FreeStringBuffer(&strBuf)` calls at lines 638, 643 and 674, so the
`malloc`ed buffer from line 571 is never released. `PROTECT(ans)` is
unwound by the error machinery, but the raw `malloc` in the
`R_StringBuffer` is not.

`scanFrame()` (used for `what = list(...)`, i.e. `read.table()`) has the
same structure: `R_AllocStringBuffer(0, &buf)` at line 699,
`extractItem()` at lines 743/784/806, `R_FreeStringBuffer(&buf)` at line
847 — and leaks identically on error.

## Reproducer

Under an R build configured with `--enable-strict-barrier` and compiled
with `-fsanitize=address` (or run under `valgrind --leak-check=full`):

```
# scanVector path (atomic 'what'):
scan(text = "x", what = 0, quiet = TRUE)
## Error in scan(...) : scan() expected 'a real', got 'x'
##  -> leaks one 8192-byte R_StringBuffer

# scanFrame path (list 'what'; also what read.table uses):
scan(text = "x", what = list(0), quiet = TRUE)

# reachable from read.table()/read.csv() when a column is typed numeric.
# (With the default colClasses the fields are read as character, so there
# is no conversion error and no leak; forcing a numeric column triggers it.)
read.csv(text = "value\nx", colClasses = "numeric")
```

Each failed call leaks 8192 bytes. Repeating it grows RSS without bound.

## Sanitizer output

```
==ERROR: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks

Direct leak of 8192 byte(s) in 1 object(s) allocated from:
    #0 ... in malloc
    #1 ... in R_AllocStringBuffer src/main/memory.c:4969
    #2 ... in scanVector       src/main/scan.c:571
    #3 ... in do_scan          src/main/scan.c:1001
    #4 ... in bcEval_loop      src/main/eval.c:8150
    #5 ... in bcEval           src/main/eval.c:7533
    #6 ... in Rf_eval          src/main/eval.c:1167
    #7 ... in R_execClosure    src/main/eval.c:2398
    ...

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: 8192 byte(s) leaked in 1 allocation(s).
```

## Suggested fix

`do_scan()` already installs an on-error cleanup for the same call: it
sets up a context whose `cend` handler, `scan_cleanup()`, releases the
connection and the `quoteset` buffer on a non-local exit:

```
begincontext(&cntxt, CTXT_CCODE, R_GlobalContext->call, R_BaseEnv,
             R_BaseEnv, R_NilValue, R_NilValue);
cntxt.cend = &scan_cleanup;
cntxt.cenddata = &data;
```

The cleanest fix is to bring the string buffer under that same cleanup.
For example, add an `R_StringBuffer *buf` field to `LocalData`, point it
at the local buffer at the top of `scanVector()`/`scanFrame()`
(`d->buf = &strBuf;`), and free it in `scan_cleanup()`:

```
static void scan_cleanup(void *data)
{
    LocalData *ld = data;
    if (ld->buf) { R_FreeStringBuffer(ld->buf); ld->buf = NULL; }
    if (ld->con && !ld->ttyflag && !ld->wasopen) { ... }
    if (ld->quoteset && ld->quoteset[0]) { ... }
}
```

`R_FreeStringBuffer()` clears `buf->data`, so the existing normal-path
`R_FreeStringBuffer()` calls in `scanVector()`/`scanFrame()` become no-ops
after cleanup and there is no double free.

## How it was found

libFuzzer + AddressSanitizer harness driving `scan(text = <fuzz>, ...)`
with `what` set to `""`, `0`, and separators `,`/`\t`, embedding R via
`Rf_initEmbeddedR()`. The leak fires on essentially every input that
isn't a clean parse, so it surfaces immediately.
